methodology: The evaluation combines instrumental analytical techniques—mostly FTIR-ATR (Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy in Attenuated Total Reflection)—with the expertise of trained textile conservators.
research_objective: To establish a non-destructive, interdisciplinary protocol for studying finishing techniques and characterizing materials as well as the state of preservation of historic weighted silk textiles.

key_findings.finding: A non-destructive, minimally invasive protocol for assessing the condition and degradation of historic weighted silk was developed.
The loading process increases the weight of silk by over 100% and leads to increased hydrophilicity in tin-weighted silks.
Tensile testing is the only reliable method for evaluating fiber condition, despite weighting affecting their mechanical properties.
The fragility and deterioration of the cream-colored silk lining correlate with the weighting degree, suggesting that extreme pH baths during production might be a primary cause.

Spectral markers in FTIR-ATR spectra can be used to assess the weighting degree and calculate carbonyl content and crystallinity indices for evaluating the state of preservation of historic weighted silks.
Silk fibers diameter measured to be between 15-20 µm

Further studies carried out in the 2000s and a recent project (Safesilk) focused on metal salt-induced degradation of silk in heritage collections, shedding new light on structural changes in tin-weighted silks and its increased hydrophilicity.

properties.value: differing degrees in warp and weft
properties.context: A differing degree of weighting in the warp and weft of the same fabric provides insight into the manufacturing technique and allows differentiation between piece-weighting and skein-weighting processes.
Tensile testing appears to be the only reliable method for evaluating fiber condition, since weighting strongly affects their mechanical properties.

Visual and haptic assessment of naturally aged historical weighted silks conducted by trained conservators supports their use as reliable parameters for evaluating the condition of historic silk textiles.
